media.brief: Lumpy eba with visible dry pockets.

options.guidance: Keep pressing the lumps against the side of the bowl. They’ll smooth out.

steps.title: Shape and serve
steps.body: Wet your hands or a small bowl with cold water. Scoop out portions and shape them into smooth balls. Serve straight away with soup, or wrap each ball in cling film to keep it warm and soft.

media.alt: Hands shaping eba into a smooth ball; wrapped portions beside.
media.brief: Hands shaping eba into a smooth ball; wrapped portions beside.

tips.text: To eat: pinch a small piece, roll it into a ball, press a dent with your thumb, and scoop up the soup.

cues.see: Smooth yellow balls with a slight shine and no cracks.
cues.texture: Soft but holds its shape when you pinch off a piece.

recipes.title: Fufu
recipes.subtitle: Soft, smooth, slightly tangy cassava swallow, made on the stove with fufu flour.
recipes.story: Traditional fufu is made from fermented cassava, which takes days. In Canada and the US most families use fufu flour, and it’s excellent. Unlike eba, fufu is cooked in a pot and turned until it goes from white to smooth and stretchy.

hero.brief: Smooth, off-white balls of fufu beside a bowl of light soup. 45°.

ingredients.name: Cassava fufu flour

substitutes.name: Plantain fufu flour
substitutes.note: Same method.

ingredients.note: Look for “cassava fufu” or “fufu flour”. Plantain fufu flour works the same way.

steps.title: Mix the flour with cold water
steps.body: Off the heat, put the fufu flour in the pot. Add 1 cup of cold water and stir until there are no dry lumps. It should be a smooth, thick paste.
steps.why: Starting with cold water is what keeps fufu lump-free.

media.alt: Fufu flour and cold water mixed into a smooth paste in a pot.
media.brief: Fufu flour and cold water mixed into a smooth paste in a pot.

cues.see: A smooth, thick, off-white paste with no dry flour left.
cues.texture: Like thick pancake batter.

steps.title: Cook and turn on medium heat
steps.body: Put the pot on medium heat. Stir and turn constantly with the wooden spoon, pressing and folding. It will thicken quickly. Keep going, adding a splash of hot water if it gets too stiff.

cues.see: It changes from bright white to slightly off-white and a little see-through.
cues.texture: Smooth, soft and stretchy.

media.alt: 15-second clip: turning fufu in a pot as it turns translucent and stretchy.
media.brief: 15-second clip: turning fufu in a pot as it turns translucent and stretchy.

steps.body: Pour ¼ cup of hot water over the fufu, cover the pot, turn the heat to low and steam for 2–3 minutes. Then turn it again firmly until smooth.

recipes.title: Semolina
recipes.subtitle: The easiest swallow to start with: smooth, mild and lump-free.
recipes.story: Semolina (or “semo”) is the swallow many beginners start with: it’s quick, mild and forgiving. The only trick is to stop lumps forming, and we’ll show you how.
allergens: Wheat (gluten)

hero.brief: Smooth pale yellow semolina balls beside egusi soup. 45°.

ingredients.name: Semolina (or Semovita)
ingredients.note: Fine semolina from any supermarket works.

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.body: Bring 2½ cups of the water to a boil in the pot. Keep the rest aside.

cues.see: A full, rolling boil.
cues.hear: Loud bubbling.

steps.title: Sprinkle in the semolina while stirring
steps.body: Turn the heat to low. With one hand stirring fast, sprinkle in the semolina a little at a time with the other. Keep stirring until all of it is in.
steps.why: Adding it slowly while stirring is what prevents lumps.

media.alt: 12-second clip: sprinkling semolina into hot water while stirring quickly.
media.brief: 12-second clip: sprinkling semolina into hot water while stirring quickly.

cues.see: The semolina thickens as it goes in. Keep it moving so no lumps form.
cues.texture: It gets heavier to stir as it thickens.

steps.title: Turn until thick and smooth
steps.body: Turn and press the mixture against the side of the pot, folding it over, until it’s thick and smooth.

cues.texture: Smooth and soft, pulling away from the sides of the pot.

steps.title: Steam, then turn again
steps.body: Add the remaining ½ cup of water over the top, cover and steam on low for 3 minutes. Then turn it again for 1 minute until smooth.

recipes.title: Amala with Ewedu & Gbegiri
recipes.subtitle: Dark yam-flour swallow with silky jute-leaf soup and smooth bean soup: Ibadan’s famous “abula”.

steps.title: Gbegiri: soak and peel the beans
steps.body: Soak the beans for 30 minutes, then rub them between your palms underwater so the skins float off. Pour the skins away and repeat until mostly white (the same as our Moi Moi and Akara lessons).

steps.title: Gbegiri: blend smooth and season
steps.body: Mash the beans with a whisk, or blend them, until perfectly smooth. Return to the pot and add the palm oil, half the crayfish, the pepper, 1 stock cube and salt. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring, until smooth and pourable.

recipes.title: Beef Suya
recipes.subtitle: Thin, smoky beef skewers crusted in spicy peanut yaji, just like the street grill.
recipes.story: Suya comes from the night-time grills of Northern Nigeria. Mallams slice the beef paper-thin and press on yaji, a spice mix of ground roasted peanuts, ginger and chilli. Then they cook it over fierce heat. You don’t need a street grill: your oven’s grill (broiler) or a barbecue does it beautifully.
allergens: Peanuts
Check stock cubes: some contain wheat, soy or celery
dietary: Gluten-free if your stock cube is

hero.brief: Suya skewers with charred edges and red-brown yaji crust, sliced raw onion and tomato on the side, on newspaper-style paper. Evening light.

gallery.alt: Bowl of homemade yaji spice: fine, reddish-brown powder.
gallery.brief: Bowl of homemade yaji spice: fine, reddish-brown powder.

serveWith: Sliced raw onion, tomato and cabbage

equipment.name: Wooden or metal skewers
equipment.note: About 10. Wooden ones must soak first.

equipment.name: Oven with grill (broiler), or a barbecue
Baking tray lined with foil + wire rack
Sharp knife and board
equipment.note: A sharp knife makes thin slices easy.

equipment.name: Blender or spice grinder
equipment.note: Only if you’re grinding peanuts yourself.

ingredients.name: Beef sirloin, rump or flank steak
ingredients.note: A tender steak cut. Suya cooks fast, so tough stewing beef won’t soften in time.

substitutes.name: Boneless chicken thighs
substitutes.note: Slice thin the same way. Cook 1–2 minutes longer per side.

ingredients.name: Kuli-kuli powder (ground roasted peanut)
ingredients.note: The base of yaji. It gives the nutty crust.

substitutes.name: Unsalted roasted peanuts, ground
substitutes.note: Pulse in short bursts until powdery. Stop before it turns into peanut butter.

ingredients.name: Smoked paprika
ingredients.note: Gives colour and a smoky taste even in an oven.

substitutes.name: Sweet paprika
substitutes.note: Same amount.

ingredients.name: Cayenne pepper (or ground dried chilli)
ingredients.note: 1 tsp for warm, 2 tsp for fiery.

steps.title: Soak the skewers and chill the beef
steps.body: If you’re using wooden skewers, put them in a tray of water to soak. Put the beef in the freezer at the same time.
steps.why: Soaked skewers don’t burn under the grill. Slightly frozen beef is firm, so you can slice it very thin easily.

media.alt: Wooden skewers soaking in a tray of water; beef on a plate going into the freezer.
media.brief: Wooden skewers soaking in a tray of water; beef on a plate going into the freezer.

cues.see: Wooden skewers under water and the beef firming up in the freezer.
cues.texture: After 30–45 minutes the beef is firm at the edges but not frozen solid.

steps.title: Slice the beef thinly
steps.body: Look at the beef for the thin lines running through it (the “grain”). Slice across those lines, not along them, into strips about 3–5 mm thick, roughly the thickness of two coins stacked. Then cut long strips into pieces about the length of your hand.
steps.why: Thin slices cook quickly and stay tender. Cutting across the grain keeps them from being chewy.

cues.see: Thin, even strips you can almost see light through at the edges.

media.alt: 15-second clip: slicing chilled beef across the grain into thin, even strips.

recipes.story: This is the chicken that sits next to jollof at every party. The flavour goes all the way through because the chicken is seasoned and cooked in its own juices before it’s fried. Then it gets coated in a sweet-hot pepper sauce.

steps.title: Prepare the chicken
steps.body: Take the chicken out of the packet and pat it dry with paper towels. Trim off any large flaps of loose fat with a knife or kitchen scissors. Wash your hands, the board and the knife with hot soapy water afterwards.
steps.why: We don’t rinse raw chicken under the tap. The water splashes germs around your sink. Cooking makes it safe.

steps.title: Season the chicken and let it rest
steps.body: Blend or finely grate the onion, garlic and ginger. Put the chicken in a large bowl. Add the blended onion mix, thyme, curry powder, 2 crumbled stock cubes and the salt. Rub it all over every piece with your hands. Cover and leave it for 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge for even more flavour.

tips.text: At Mcuire we season the night before. If you can plan ahead, do it. The flavour goes right to the bone.

steps.title: Cook the chicken in its own juices
steps.body: Put the chicken and all the seasoning into the pot. Add ½ cup of water. Cover and cook on medium heat, turning the pieces once halfway, until the chicken is cooked all the way through.

cues.see: Chicken turns white all over and the juices around it are clear, not pink.

media.alt: Cooked chicken in the pot with clear, golden juices.
media.brief: Cooked chicken in the pot with clear, golden juices.

tips.text: Cut into the thickest piece next to the bone. No pink, and the juices are clear. With a thermometer, it reads 74°C (165°F).
Save the liquid in the pot. It’s a delicious stock for the pepper sauce, or for jollof.

steps.title: Dry the chicken
steps.body: Lift the chicken out onto a tray. Pat each piece dry with paper towels and leave it to cool for 5 minutes. Pour the cooking liquid into a cup and keep it.
steps.why: Wet chicken makes hot oil spit. Dry chicken fries crispier and more safely.

cues.see: Dry, cooked chicken pieces on a tray, and a cup of golden stock kept aside.

steps.title: Fry until golden (or bake)
steps.body:
Pour oil into the deep pan to about 2–3 cm deep and heat it on medium-high. Test it by dipping the handle of a wooden spoon in. When steady bubbles rise around it, the oil is ready (about 175°C). Gently lay in a few pieces, away from you, without crowding. Fry 4–6 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp. Lift onto paper towels. Repeat with the rest.

No frying? Bake on a lined tray at 220°C (425°F) for 20–25 minutes, turning once, until golden.

cues.hear: A lively, steady sizzle.
cues.see: Deep golden-brown, crisp skin.

media.brief: 15-second clip: laying chicken into hot oil away from the body, then turning golden pieces with tongs.

tips.text: Never leave hot oil alone, and never put water on an oil fire. If it flames, cover it with a lid and turn off the heat.
Fry in batches. Too many pieces at once cools the oil and makes them greasy instead of crisp.

recipes.title: Puff-Puff
recipes.subtitle: Soft, fluffy, lightly sweet fried dough balls, golden outside and airy inside.
recipes.story: Puff-puff is the snack that disappears first at every party. It has just a handful of pantry ingredients and one technique: shaping the batter with your hand. We’ll show you the batter texture and the drop until you have it.
allergens: Wheat (gluten)

hero.brief: A bowl heaped with round golden puff-puff, one broken open to show the fluffy inside. Natural light.

gallery.alt: Risen puff-puff batter: doubled, bubbly, stretchy on a spoon.
gallery.brief: Risen puff-puff batter: doubled, bubbly, stretchy on a spoon.

equipment.name: Cling film or clean tea towel
equipment.note: To cover the batter while it rises.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: Use a little less for a less sweet puff-puff.

ingredients.name: Instant (fast-action) yeast
ingredients.note: One standard sachet.

substitutes.name: Active dry yeast
substitutes.note: Same amount. Stir it into the warm water first and wait 5 minutes until foamy.

ingredients.name: Warm water
ingredients.note: Warm like a comfortable bath, not hot.

steps.title: Get the water just warm
steps.body: Mix hot and cold water until it feels comfortably warm on the inside of your wrist, like a nice bath. Not hot.
steps.why: Yeast is alive. Water that’s too hot kills it and your puff-puff won’t rise.

cues.texture: Pleasantly warm on your wrist. If you’re using a thermometer, about 40°C (105°F).

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.body: In the large bowl, mix the flour, sugar, yeast, salt and nutmeg with a spoon until evenly combined.

media.alt: Flour, sugar, yeast and nutmeg in a large bowl, mixed.
media.brief: Flour, sugar, yeast and nutmeg in a large bowl, mixed.

cues.see: An even mix of flour, sugar and yeast with no streaks.

steps.title: Add the water and beat the batter
steps.body: Pour in the warm water. Mix with your clean hand or a wooden spoon, scooping up from the bottom and slapping it back down, for 3–5 minutes until the batter is smooth with no dry flour.
steps.why: Beating builds stretch in the batter. That’s what gives puff-puff its soft, chewy inside.

cues.texture: Thick, smooth, sticky and stretchy. It falls slowly from the spoon in a thick ribbon.

media.alt: 15-second clip: beating the batter by hand, then lifting to show the thick, stretchy ribbon.
media.brief: 15-second clip: beating the batter by hand, then lifting to show the thick, stretchy ribbon.

checkpoint.question: How does your batter fall from the spoon?

media.brief: Batter too stiff: clumps on the spoon.

options.guidance: Mix in warm water, 2 tablespoons at a time.

options.label: Thick ribbon, falls slowly

media.brief: Correct batter: thick, slow ribbon from spoon.

media.brief: Batter too runny: pours quickly.

steps.title: Let the batter rise
steps.body: Cover the bowl with cling film or a tea towel and put it somewhere warm, away from draughts. Leave it until it has doubled in size and the top is full of bubbles.

cues.see: Doubled in size, puffy, with lots of bubbles on top.
cues.smell: Slightly sweet and yeasty, like bread.

media.alt: Before and after: batter at the start vs doubled and bubbly.
media.brief: Before and after: batter at the start vs doubled and bubbly.

tips.text: A cold kitchen? Put the bowl in your oven with only the light switched on. It makes a perfect warm spot.

options.label: Barely changed

media.alt: Batter that hasn’t risen.
media.brief: Batter that hasn’t risen.

options.guidance: Give it another 15–20 minutes somewhere warmer. If nothing happens after an hour, your yeast may be old or the water was too hot.

options.label: Doubled and bubbly

media.alt: Batter doubled with bubbles.
media.brief: Batter doubled with bubbles.

options.guidance: Ready to fry. Give it one quick stir to knock out large bubbles.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.body: Pour oil into the deep pot until it’s about 6–8 cm deep, and heat on medium. Test by dropping in a tiny bit of batter. It should sink slightly, then rise to the top and sizzle steadily within 3–4 seconds (about 170°C).

tips.text: If the test piece browns in seconds, the oil is too hot. Your puff-puff would be dark outside and raw inside. Turn it down and wait 2 minutes.
Never leave hot oil alone. Keep a lid nearby. If it ever catches fire, cover it and turn off the heat. Never use water.

cues.see: A test drop sinks slightly, then rises and sizzles steadily.
cues.hear: A steady, gentle sizzle. Violent bubbling means the oil is too hot.

steps.title: Shape and drop the balls
steps.body: Wet your hand with water. Scoop up some batter, close your fist gently, and squeeze so a small ball of batter pushes out between your thumb and first finger. Scrape it off with a spoon and let it drop gently into the oil, close to the surface. Repeat, leaving space between them.

media.alt: Shaping puff-puff balls
media.brief: 20-second clip: squeezing batter through the fist, scraping a round ball into the oil. Slow and clear.

tips.text: Not comfortable using your hand? Use two spoons: scoop with one, push off with the other. They’ll be less round, but just as tasty.
Dip your hand (or spoons) in water between drops so the batter doesn’t stick.

cues.see: Round balls of batter dropping in and puffing up, with space between them.
cues.hear: A soft sizzle as each ball goes in.

steps.title: Fry until golden all over
steps.body: Fry until golden on the bottom. Many will roll over on their own; turn the rest with the slotted spoon. Fry until evenly golden-brown all over.

cues.see: Round, puffed and evenly golden-brown.

recipes.title: Akara
recipes.subtitle: Crisp, golden bean fritters, fluffy inside, spiked with onion and pepper.
recipes.story: Akara is the classic Saturday-morning street breakfast, fried fresh at the roadside and eaten with pap or bread. It uses the same peeled beans as moi moi, but blended very thick and whipped with air so it puffs up in the oil.
allergens: Check stock cubes: some contain wheat, soy or celery
dietary: Gluten-free if your stock cube is

substitutes.name: Peeled bean flour (akara flour)

steps.body: Cover the beans with plenty of cold water and leave them to soak so the skins loosen.

steps.title: Peel the beans
steps.body: Rub handfuls of beans firmly between your palms under the water. The skins float. Pour them off, add fresh water and repeat until the beans are mostly white. (Or pulse the soaked beans 2–3 times in the blender with water to crack the skins, then float them off.)

steps.body: Drain the beans well. Blend them with as little water as possible, starting with just 3–4 tablespoons and adding more only if the blender is stuck. Stop the blender and push the mix down with a spoon as needed.
steps.why: This is the big difference from moi moi. Akara batter must be thick. Watery batter spreads flat in the oil and soaks up grease.

steps.body: Tip the paste into a bowl. Beat it hard with a wooden spoon or whisk, in a circular folding motion, for 3–5 minutes (2 minutes with an electric whisk).
steps.why: Whipping traps air, and the air is what makes akara puff up light and fluffy.

cues.hear: A steady sizzle, not a roar.

recipes.title: Fried Plantain (Dodo)
recipes.subtitle: Sweet, caramelised plantain with crisp edges and a soft centre.
recipes.story: Dodo is simple, but most of the result is decided before you light the stove: by how ripe your plantain is and how thick you cut it. Get those right and it caramelises perfectly every time.

steps.body: Mix the flour, baking powder and salt. Add the cold butter and rub it in with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs. Add the cold water a little at a time, mixing with a knife or your hand, just until it comes together as a dough. Don’t knead it much.

steps.body: Wrap the dough in cling film and chill it in the fridge. Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) in the meantime.

steps.title: Roll and cut circles
steps.body: On a floured counter, roll the dough to about 3–4 mm thick. Cut circles about 12–13 cm across with a cutter, saucer or small bowl. Re-roll the scraps once.

steps.body: Put about 1½ tablespoons of cooled filling on one half of each circle. Brush the edge with beaten egg, fold the pastry over and press the edges together. Crimp the edge firmly with a fork, then prick the top twice to let steam out.

steps.body: Put the pies on lined trays, brush the tops with beaten egg and bake until deep golden.

recipes.title: Chin Chin
recipes.subtitle: Crunchy, lightly sweet little fried dough bites with a hint of nutmeg.
recipes.story: Chin chin is the snack in every Nigerian party pack and on every coffee table at Christmas. It’s a simple dough, rolled, cut into small squares and fried until crunchy. It keeps for weeks, so make a big batch.
allergens: Wheat (gluten)
Eggs
Milk

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.body: Cover the dough with cling film or a bowl and let it rest.

steps.title: Roll and cut into small squares

recipes.title: Moi Moi
recipes.subtitle: Silky, savoury steamed bean pudding with peppers, egg and fish.
recipes.story: Moi moi is steamed blended beans, rich with peppers and oil. It’s served at parties next to jollof and at breakfast with pap. The two skills are peeling the beans and getting the batter to the right thickness. We’ll walk you through both.
allergens: Eggs (optional)
Fish and shellfish (crayfish, fish, optional)
Check stock cubes: some contain wheat, soy or celery
dietary: Gluten-free if your stock cubes are
Vegan without egg, fish and crayfish

hero.brief: Moi moi turned out of a ramekin, cut open to show smooth orange inside with slices of boiled egg. 45°.

gallery.alt: Peeled white beans next to beans with skins on.
gallery.brief: Peeled white beans next to beans with skins on.

equipment.name: Large bowl
equipment.note: For soaking and peeling the beans.

equipment.name: Blender
equipment.note: A powerful one gives the smoothest moi moi.

equipment.name: 6–8 ramekins, foil cups or heatproof bowls
equipment.note: Or traditional moi moi leaves (uma leaves).

equipment.name: Small rack or a crumpled sheet of foil
equipment.note: To keep the containers off the bottom of the pot.

ingredients.name: Black-eyed beans or Nigerian brown beans (dry)
ingredients.note: Black-eyed peas are in most supermarkets. Nigerian brown (honey) beans are sweeter.

substitutes.name: Peeled bean flour (moi moi / akara flour)
substitutes.note: Skips soaking and peeling. Use about 2 cups and mix with liquid as in step 4.

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil or palm oil
ingredients.note: Oil makes moi moi soft and silky. Don’t reduce it too much.

ingredients.name: Warm stock or water
ingredients.note: Add it gradually. You may not need all of it.

steps.title: Soak the beans
steps.body: Put the beans in a large bowl and cover with plenty of cold water. Leave them to soak so the skins loosen.

cues.see: Beans slightly swollen, with skins starting to wrinkle.

media.alt: Black-eyed beans soaking in a bowl, skins wrinkling.
media.brief: Black-eyed beans soaking in a bowl, skins wrinkling.

tips.text: Using peeled bean flour? Skip to step 3. It saves about an hour.

steps.title: Peel the beans
steps.body:
Grab a handful of beans and rub them firmly between your palms under the water, as if you’re warming your hands. The skins will come off and float. Tip the floating skins away, add fresh water and repeat until almost all the beans are white.

Faster way: put the soaked beans in the blender with water and pulse 2–3 times, just to crack them. The skins float off when you add more water.
steps.why: Skins make moi moi grainy and grey. Peeled beans give that silky, orange finish.

media.alt: 20-second clip: rubbing beans between palms underwater; skins floating to the top and being poured off.
media.brief: 20-second clip: rubbing beans between palms underwater; skins floating to the top and being poured off.

options.label: Lots of dark skins left

media.alt: Half-peeled beans, many dark skins.
media.brief: Half-peeled beans, many dark skins.

options.guidance: Keep rubbing and rinsing. Change the water each round.

options.label: Mostly white, a few skins

media.alt: Correctly peeled beans, mostly white.
media.brief: Correctly peeled beans, mostly white.

options.guidance: Perfect. A few skins are fine.

cues.see: Almost all the beans are white, with the brown skins floating off.

steps.title: Blend until completely smooth
steps.body: Drain the beans. Roughly chop the peppers and onion. Blend everything with just enough water to keep the blender moving, about ½ cup to start. Blend in two batches if needed, until perfectly smooth.

cues.texture: Smooth like thick custard. Rub a little between your fingers: it shouldn’t feel gritty.

media.alt: Smooth orange bean batter pouring from the blender.
media.brief: Smooth orange bean batter pouring from the blender.

checkpoint.question: Rub some between your fingers. How does it feel?

options.label: Gritty or grainy

media.alt: Grainy bean batter.
media.brief: Grainy bean batter.

options.guidance: Blend for another 1–2 minutes. Add a splash of water if the blender is struggling.

options.label: Silky smooth

media.alt: Silky smooth bean batter.
media.brief: Silky smooth bean batter.

options.guidance: Perfect.

steps.title: Season and loosen the batter
steps.body: Pour the batter into a big bowl. Stir in the oil, crayfish, crumbled stock cubes and salt. Now add the warm stock a little at a time, stirring well, until it pours slowly off the spoon.
steps.why: The thickness decides the texture. Too thick and moi moi comes out hard and dry; too thin and it won’t set.

cues.texture: Like thick pancake batter: it pours off the spoon slowly and smoothly.
cues.see: Bright orange and glossy from the oil.

media.alt: Mixing the moi moi batter
media.brief: 10-second clip: lifting a spoon from the seasoned batter to show it pouring slowly.

tips.text: Don’t taste the raw batter. Raw beans can upset your stomach. Measure the seasoning instead. You can adjust next time.

options.label: Thick paste, barely moves

media.alt: Batter too thick, sitting on the spoon.
media.brief: Batter too thick, sitting on the spoon.

options.guidance: Add more warm stock, 2 tablespoons at a time.

options.label: Pours slowly like pancake batter

media.alt: Correct moi moi batter consistency.
media.brief: Correct moi moi batter consistency.

options.guidance: Perfect.

options.label: Runs like soup

media.alt: Batter too thin, runny.
media.brief: Batter too thin, runny.

options.guidance: Too thin. Stir in a few tablespoons of bean flour (or blend a few more soaked beans). Otherwise it may not set.

steps.title: Fill the containers
steps.body: Lightly oil each container. Fill them about three-quarters full (it rises a little). Push a slice of egg and a little fish into each one. Cover each tightly with a piece of foil.

media.alt: Moi moi wrapped for steaming
media.brief: Ramekins filled ¾ with orange batter, egg slices pushed in, foil being pressed over.

cues.see: Containers three-quarters full of orange batter, with egg and fish pushed in, and foil tightly on top.

steps.title: Steam the moi moi
steps.body: Put the rack or crumpled foil in the bottom of your big pot and arrange the containers on it. Carefully pour boiling water into the pot until it comes about halfway up the sides of the containers. Cover the pot and steam on medium-low.

cues.hear: A gentle bubbling under the lid. Not a hard, rattling boil.

media.alt: Covered ramekins standing in a pot with water halfway up their sides.
media.brief: Covered ramekins standing in a pot with water halfway up their sides.

tips.text: Check the water every 15 minutes and top up with boiling water from the kettle. If the pot boils dry, the bottoms will burn.

steps.title: Check that it’s set
steps.body: Lift the foil off one container (watch out for steam) and push a knife or skewer into the centre, then pull it out.

cues.texture: Firm and springy when pressed, like a set custard.

media.alt: Clean knife pulled out of a set moi moi.
media.brief: Clean knife pulled out of a set moi moi.

options.label: Wet batter sticks to it

media.alt: Knife with wet batter on it.
media.brief: Knife with wet batter on it.

options.guidance: Not set yet. Re-cover and steam for 10–15 more minutes, then check again.

options.label: Comes out clean

media.alt: Clean knife from a set moi moi.
media.brief: Clean knife from a set moi moi.

options.guidance: It’s done. Turn off the heat.

steps.title: Rest, turn out and serve
steps.body: Leave the moi moi to rest in the pot for 10 minutes. It firms up as it cools slightly. Run a knife around the edge and turn it out onto a plate, or serve it right in the container.

media.alt: Mcuire plating: moi moi turned out next to jollof and dodo.
media.brief: Mcuire plating: moi moi turned out next to jollof and dodo.

tips.text: Moi moi freezes beautifully for up to 2 months. Reheat by steaming for 15 minutes.

cues.see: A smooth, orange-red block that slides out clean.
cues.texture: Firm and springy, like a soft cake.

recipes.title: Kelewele
recipes.subtitle: Ghana’s spicy fried plantain: tossed in ginger, garlic and pepper, then fried until caramelised.
recipes.story: Kelewele (say “keh-leh-weh-leh”) is Ghana’s favourite night-time street snack: chunks of ripe plantain tossed in a fiery ginger-spice paste and fried until sticky and caramelised. It’s usually eaten with roasted peanuts.

hero.brief: Caramelised, spice-coated plantain cubes in a paper cone with roasted peanuts. Evening light.

serveWith: On its own as a snack

ingredients.name: Ripe plantains (yellow with black spots, still firm)
ingredients.note: Ripe but firm. Very soft plantain falls apart when tossed.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.note: Ginger is the main flavour, so don’t be shy.

ingredients.name: Scotch bonnet peppers

substitutes.name: Habanero
substitutes.note: Same heat and fruity flavour.

ingredients.note: Use fewer, or remove the seeds, for less heat.

steps.title: Peel and cut the plantain
steps.body: Cut off the ends, slit the skin along a ridge and peel. Cut into bite-size cubes, about 2 cm, or diagonal chunks.

media.alt: Peeled plantain cut into even 2 cm cubes.
media.brief: Peeled plantain cut into even 2 cm cubes.

cues.see: Even 2 cm cubes of golden-yellow plantain.

steps.title: Make the spice paste
steps.body: Blend or finely grate the ginger, garlic, onion and scotch bonnet with the cloves, nutmeg, salt and 1 tablespoon of water to a paste.

media.alt: Ginger-pepper spice paste in a small bowl.
media.brief: Ginger-pepper spice paste in a small bowl.

tips.text: Wash your hands with soap after cutting scotch bonnet, and keep them away from your eyes.

steps.title: Toss and rest
steps.body: Toss the plantain with the spice paste until every piece is coated. Leave it for 15 minutes to soak up the flavour.

media.alt: 8-second clip: tossing plantain cubes in the spice paste.

cues.see: Every cube coated in a reddish spice paste.

steps.title: Heat the oil

tips.text: Never leave hot oil alone. Keep a lid nearby. If it ever catches fire, cover it and turn off the heat. Never use water.

cues.see: A test piece sizzles straight away.
cues.hear: A steady sizzle.

steps.title: Fry until caramelised
steps.body: Fry in batches, turning, until deep golden-brown with dark, sticky edges.

cues.see: Deep golden with dark caramelised edges.

media.alt: Kelewele frying, edges darkening.
media.brief: Kelewele frying, edges darkening.

options.label: Pale yellow

media.alt: Pale kelewele.
media.brief: Pale kelewele.

options.guidance: Another minute or two.

options.label: Deep golden, caramelised

media.alt: Perfect kelewele.
media.brief: Perfect kelewele.

options.guidance: Perfect. Out they come.

options.label: Black spots

media.alt: Burnt kelewele.
media.brief: Burnt kelewele.

options.guidance: The spice paste burns quickly. Lower the heat a little for the next batch.

steps.title: Drain and serve
steps.body: Drain on paper towels and serve warm with a handful of roasted peanuts.

media.alt: Mcuire kelewele in a paper cone with peanuts.
media.brief: Mcuire kelewele in a paper cone with peanuts.

recipes.title: Jollof + Chicken + Plantain
recipes.subtitle: The classic Nigerian party plate, timed so all three are hot at the same moment.
recipes.story: Cooking one dish is a recipe. Cooking three at once is a plan. This lesson is the plan: what to start when, what can wait, and how to use the hands-off moments so nothing goes cold.

hero.brief: The Mcuire party plate: jollof, glossy peppered chicken, dodo, a little salad. 45°.

steps.title: Shop, and season the chicken the night before
steps.body: Add this meal to your shopping list and everything for all three dishes is added at once. If you can, season the chicken the night before (Peppered Chicken, steps 1–2) and keep it in the fridge. It saves 30 minutes and tastes better.

tips.text: Make sure your plantains are yellow with black spots. If they’re green, buy them 4–7 days ahead.

cues.see: Everything for all three dishes on your list, and seasoned chicken resting in the fridge.

steps.title: 2 hr 30 before: start the chicken and the jollof base
steps.body: Not seasoned yet? Season the chicken now and let it rest (Peppered Chicken, step 2). At the same time, blend the jollof pepper base and start boiling it down (Jollof, steps 1–3).

cues.see: Seasoned chicken resting, and the jollof pepper base starting to bubble.

steps.title: 2 hr before: cook the chicken while frying the jollof base
steps.body: Put the chicken on to cook in its own juices (Peppered Chicken, step 3). While it cooks, wash the rice and fry the onion, tomato paste and pepper base for the jollof until the oil rises (Jollof, steps 4–7).

tips.text: Use some of the chicken’s cooking liquid as the stock for your jollof. That’s how restaurants do it.

cues.see: Chicken simmering in its juices, and red oil rising on the jollof base.

steps.title: 1 hr 20 before: rice in, lid on, now fry the chicken
steps.body: Season the jollof sauce, add the rice, cover with foil and steam on low (Jollof, steps 8–10). You now have about 30 hands-off minutes. Use them to dry and fry the chicken (or bake it), and make the pepper sauce (Peppered Chicken, steps 4–6).

tips.text: Don’t lift the jollof lid while you’re busy with the chicken. Trust the timer.

cues.see: The jollof sealed under foil on low, and the chicken frying golden while you wait.

steps.title: 35 min before: finish the jollof, toss the chicken
steps.body: Check and turn the jollof, then give it the smoky party finish (Jollof, steps 11–12). Turn the pepper sauce to low and toss the fried chicken in it (Peppered Chicken, step 7). Leave it covered on the lowest heat.

cues.see: Jollof grains turned and nearly done, and the chicken coated in glossy red sauce.

steps.title: 15 min before: fry the dodo while the jollof rests
steps.body: Turn off the jollof and let it rest, covered (Jollof, step 13). Now peel, slice and fry the plantain (Dodo, steps 2–5). Dodo is best fresh, so it goes last.

cues.see: Jollof resting, covered, while plantain slices turn golden in the pan.

steps.title: Plate it the Mcuire way
steps.body: Spoon a generous mound of jollof onto one side of the plate. Lean a piece or two of peppered chicken against it, spooning over a little sauce. Fan 4–5 slices of dodo on the other side. Add a little coleslaw or sliced tomato and cucumber for freshness.

media.alt: Step-by-step plating: jollof mound, chicken leaning, dodo fanned, salad.
media.brief: Step-by-step plating: jollof mound, chicken leaning, dodo fanned, salad.

checkpoint.question: Is everything hot and ready together?

options.label: All hot at once

media.alt: Three dishes ready on the counter at once.
media.brief: Three dishes ready on the counter at once.

options.guidance: You just cooked a party plate. That’s real confidence in the kitchen.

options.label: Something went cold

media.alt: Reheating chicken in a hot oven.
media.brief: Reheating chicken in a hot oven.

options.guidance: Warm chicken for 8 minutes in a 200°C oven, and jollof covered on low with a splash of water. Next time, start the chicken 15 minutes later.

cues.see: A mound of red-orange jollof, glossy peppered chicken leaning against it, and a fan of golden dodo.

recipes.title: Egusi + Pounded Yam
recipes.subtitle: Soup and swallow, the way it’s served at a Mcuire table.
recipes.story: Pounded yam has to be made at the very last minute, while the soup waits happily on low heat. This plan shows you how to get them to the table together, piping hot.

hero.brief: Egusi in a bowl beside a smooth mound of pounded yam on a Mcuire plate. 45°.

steps.title: 2 hr before: start the meat
steps.body: Season and steam the meat, then simmer until tender (Egusi, steps 1–3). While it simmers, soak the fish, blend the peppers and mix the egusi paste (Egusi, steps 4–6).

cues.see: Meat simmering, fish soaking, peppers blended and the egusi paste mixed.

steps.title: 1 hr 10 before: cook the soup
steps.body: Fry the egusi lumps in palm oil, add the peppers and stock, then the meat and fish, and simmer (Egusi, steps 7–11).

cues.see: Golden egusi lumps in a red-orange soup with oil rising.

steps.title: 45 min before: peel and boil the yam
steps.body: While the soup simmers, peel and cut the yam and put it on to boil (Pounded Yam, steps 1–2).

tips.text: Set up your food processor now, so it’s ready the moment the yam is soft.

cues.see: White yam chunks boiling while the soup simmers.

steps.title: 15 min before: greens in, soup on low
steps.body: Stir the greens into the egusi (Egusi, step 12), then turn the soup to the lowest heat and cover it. It will happily wait.

cues.see: Bright green leaves through the soup, and the pot on its lowest heat.

steps.title: 10 min before: pound the yam
steps.body: Drain the yam and pound it while it’s very hot, then shape it into balls (Pounded Yam, steps 3–5).

tips.text: Swallow is always last. Soup can wait; pounded yam can’t.

cues.see: Smooth, white balls of pounded yam.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Ladle egusi into deep bowls with plenty of meat and fish. Put a ball of pounded yam on a plate beside each bowl. Put a bowl of water on the table for washing hands: it’s traditional to eat this with your right hand.

media.alt: Table set with egusi, pounded yam and a hand-washing bowl.
media.brief: Table set with egusi, pounded yam and a hand-washing bowl.

cues.see: Bowls of golden egusi with meat and fish, smooth pounded yam beside each one, and a water bowl for washing hands.

recipes.title: Rice + Stew + Protein
recipes.subtitle: Cook once on Sunday, eat well all week. A meal-prep plan with Nigerian stew.
recipes.story: A big pot of stew is the backbone of a Nigerian kitchen. Cook it once and it becomes rice and stew, stew with yam, stew with plantain and beans… This plan doubles the stew, portions it and gives you a week of quick dinners.

hero.brief: Meal-prep containers of rice and red stew with chicken, a pot of stew behind. Overhead.

steps.title: Choose your batch size
steps.body: Set the servings above to the number of meals you want for the week (10 is about 5 days for 2 people). Add this meal to your shopping list and the quantities scale automatically.

tips.text: You’ll need your largest pot. If it’s more than half full, split the stew between two pots.

cues.see: The shopping list showing quantities for your chosen batch size.

steps.title: Cook the chicken and the stew base together
steps.body: Cook the chicken in its juices while you blend and boil down the stew base (Rice & Stew, steps 1–3).

cues.see: Chicken simmering in its juices, and the stew base reducing in another pot.

steps.title: Fry the stew slowly
steps.body: Fry the chicken if you like, then fry the paste and the stew base until the oil rises (Rice & Stew, steps 4–6). A big batch takes 5–10 minutes longer. Wait for the oil.

cues.see: Red oil rising to the top of the stew.
cues.hear: Thick “plop” bubbles.

steps.title: Cook the rice and finish the stew
steps.body: Cook the rice while the stew finishes with the stock and chicken (Rice & Stew, steps 7–8).

cues.see: Fluffy white rice and a thick, glossy stew with the chicken.

steps.title: Cool quickly and portion
steps.body: Spread the rice on a tray to cool, and pour the stew into a wide dish so it cools faster. Within 2 hours of cooking, divide into containers: rice, a ladle of stew and one piece of chicken each. Refrigerate what you’ll eat in the next 3 days and freeze the rest.
steps.why: Cooling quickly and refrigerating within 2 hours keeps cooked rice safe to eat later.

media.alt: Portioning rice, stew and chicken into containers.
media.brief: Portioning rice, stew and chicken into containers.

tips.text: Reheat rice until steaming hot all the way through, and only reheat it once.

cues.see: Rice spread thin on a tray, stew in a wide dish, then neat containers ready for the fridge.

steps.title: On the day: add fresh dodo
steps.body: Reheat a container until steaming hot. Fry a fresh plantain in 10 minutes (Dodo lesson) and you have a full Mcuire plate on a weeknight.

tips.text: Leftover stew also turns into a new meal: serve it with boiled yam, with beans and plantain, or with fried eggs and bread.

cues.see: Steaming hot rice and stew, with fresh golden dodo on the side.

recipes.title: West African Sunday Dinner
recipes.subtitle: Fried rice, peppered chicken, moi moi and dodo: a full family table, planned from morning to plate.
recipes.story: Sunday dinner is about the whole table. The trick is that two dishes, moi moi and seasoned chicken, can be done in the morning, so the afternoon is calm and dinner arrives together.

hero.brief: A family table: fried rice, peppered chicken, moi moi turned out, dodo, coleslaw, drinks. Overhead.

steps.title: Morning: soak the beans and season the chicken
steps.body: Put the beans to soak (Moi Moi, step 1) and season the chicken, then put it in the fridge (Peppered Chicken, steps 1–2).

cues.see: Beans soaking and seasoned chicken in the fridge.

steps.title: Late morning: make and steam the moi moi
steps.body: Peel and blend the beans, mix the batter, fill the containers and steam them (Moi Moi, steps 2–7). Once set, let them cool in the pot. They reheat perfectly later.

tips.text: Making moi moi first means the hardest dish is done before lunch.

cues.see: Set moi moi in their containers, cooling in the pot.

steps.title: 3 hr before: cook the curry rice and cool it
steps.body: Cook the rice in curry stock and spread it out to cool (Fried Rice, steps 1–3). Then chop all the vegetables.

tips.text: Rice cooked early and cooled makes the best fried rice.

cues.see: Yellow curry rice spread out to cool, and all the vegetables diced.

steps.title: 2 hr before: cook and fry the chicken
steps.body: Cook the chicken in its juices, dry it, and fry (or bake) it (Peppered Chicken, steps 3–5). Make the pepper sauce but don’t toss yet (step 6).

cues.see: Golden fried chicken, and the pepper sauce ready on the side.

steps.title: 45 min before: fry the rice
steps.body: Cook the prawns and liver, stir-fry the vegetables, then fry the rice in batches (Fried Rice, steps 4–7). Cover the dish with foil and keep it in a low oven (90°C).

cues.see: Golden fried rice under foil, kept warm in the oven.

steps.title: 20 min before: reheat moi moi, toss chicken, fry dodo
steps.body: Put the moi moi back on to steam for 15 minutes. Toss the chicken in the warm pepper sauce (Peppered Chicken, step 7). Fry the dodo last (Dodo, steps 2–5).

cues.see: Moi moi steaming, chicken coated in sauce, and dodo frying last.

steps.title: Set the table
steps.body: Serve everything family-style in the middle of the table: fried rice in a big dish, chicken piled high, moi moi turned out onto a plate, dodo in a bowl, and a fresh salad or coleslaw.

media.alt: Family-style table layout from above.
media.brief: Family-style table layout from above.

cues.see: A full table: fried rice, a pile of chicken, moi moi, dodo and fresh salad.

recipes.title: Party Platter for 20
recipes.subtitle: Small chops, jollof, fried rice and grills for a crowd, with a two-day timing plan.
recipes.story: Feeding twenty people is about planning, not panic. Half of this menu can be made the day before. This is the order we’d use in the Mcuire kitchen for a big celebration.

hero.brief: A full party table: trays of jollof and fried rice, chicken, suya, moi moi, puff-puff, dodo, chin chin. Overhead.

steps.title: A week before: plan, shop and make chin chin
steps.body: Add this meal to your shopping list for 20 people. Check you have big enough pots. You’ll want two pots for the jollof (rice cooks unevenly in one giant pot). Make the chin chin now: it keeps for weeks in a sealed container.

tips.text: Ask one friend to help on the day just with frying. It changes everything.

cues.see: Your shopping list for 20, two big pots ready, and a sealed jar of chin chin.

steps.title: The day before: bases, seasoning and moi moi
steps.body: Blend and boil down the jollof pepper base (Jollof, steps 2–3) and refrigerate it. Season the chicken (Peppered Chicken, steps 1–2) and the suya beef (Suya, steps 1–4) and refrigerate them. Make and steam the moi moi (Moi Moi lesson). It reheats perfectly.

cues.see: Jollof base in the fridge, seasoned chicken and suya beef chilling, and moi moi steamed.

steps.title: Party morning: rice dishes
steps.body: Cook and cool the curry rice for fried rice (Fried Rice, steps 1–3). Then cook the jollof in two pots, using your ready-made base (Jollof, steps 4–13). Keep the jollof covered. It holds its heat well.

cues.see: Curry rice cooling on trays, and jollof cooking in two pots.

steps.title: 3 hr before: chicken, then puff-puff batter
steps.body: Cook, fry and sauce the chicken (Peppered Chicken, steps 3–7). Mix the puff-puff batter and leave it to rise (Puff-Puff, steps 1–4).

cues.see: Chicken coated in sauce, and puff-puff batter rising under a cloth.

steps.title: 90 min before: fry the rice and puff-puff
steps.body: Finish the fried rice (Fried Rice, steps 4–7) and keep it covered in a low oven. Fry the puff-puff (Puff-Puff, steps 5–8).

cues.see: Fried rice kept warm, and trays of golden puff-puff.

steps.title: 40 min before: suya, moi moi and dodo
steps.body: Grill the suya (Suya, steps 5–8). Reheat the moi moi by steaming it for 15–20 minutes. Fry the dodo last (Dodo lesson).

cues.see: Charred suya, steaming moi moi and fresh golden dodo.

steps.title: Lay out the platter
steps.body: Serve the rice dishes side by side in large trays. Pile chicken and suya together, with onions and yaji. Put the small chops (puff-puff, chin chin, dodo, moi moi) on a separate platter, so guests can graze before the main meal.
